points.description: Mentions that the masses of one element are compared/held fixed (a fixed mass of one element, e.g. same mass of element A) when looking at different compounds, and that mass data from experiments on compounds is used.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only one of: fixed mass of one element, or use of mass data from compounds.

points.description: States that the elements combine to form different compounds and that the masses of the other element in these compounds form a ratio of small whole numbers (integer ratio).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if compounds are mentioned or a ratio is mentioned but the whole-number nature is missing or unclear.

points.description: Explains that whole-number ratios mean the element comes in discrete/indivisible units (cannot be split into fractions).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if the idea is only implied or half-stated (e.g. 'it must be in whole units').

points.description: Concludes that the indivisible unit of mass is the atom, so matter is made of atoms.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if atoms are named but not clearly linked to the indivisible unit.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the chain: fixed mass of one element and mass data in compounds, whole-number ratios, whole numbers meaning indivisible units, and those units being atoms. Any wording counts and implied links are accepted; give part marks for vague or half-stated claims. Restating the law's name or a bare definition earns nothing alone; a wrong extra remark costs nothing unless it contradicts the central idea.
